requirements.title: A derived-type specifier has a type name and an optional nonempty parameter list
requirements.source: 7.5.9, R754, R754.type-name, R754.optional-parameter-list, R754.nonempty-list; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF106, printed92.
requirements.definition: The derived-type-spec grammar is a type name optionally followed by a parenthesized, nonempty type-param-spec-list. Omitting the entire list is different from supplying empty parentheses. The named type's accessibility, parameterization, required/defaulted parameters and enclosing context impose their own constraints.

Each negative has a same-primary source-minimal conforming repair; a control may support several such contrasts and explicit admission facets. Current source/case/evidence adjudications remain separate content-bound records, not inferred from generation or observations.

requirements.title: A type-parameter specification has an optional keyword-equals prefix and a value
requirements.source: 7.5.9, R755, R755.optional-keyword, R755.keyword-equals, R755.parameter-value; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF106, printed92.
requirements.definition: A type-param-spec consists of a type-param-value, optionally preceded by keyword and equals. The keyword prefix is not a pointer-association arrow, and neither an explicit keyword nor its value can be empty. R701 owns the value alternatives; C798 and C799 own ordering and keyword membership.

requirements.title: The specifier's type name denotes an accessible derived type
requirements.source: 7.5.9, C795, C795.named-derived-type, C795.accessible-name; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF106, printed92.
requirements.definition: In a derived-type-spec, the type name must denote a derived type accessible in the relevant scope. A use alias can still denote that same definition. A data object's name is not a derived-type name merely because it is in scope. Enclosing previous-definition and type-category conditions remain.

requirements.title: Only a parameterized type can have a parameter specification list
requirements.source: 7.5.9, C796, C796.parameter-list-present, C796.parameterized-type-only; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF106, printed92.
requirements.definition: A type-param-spec-list is allowed only for a parameterized derived type. This does not require a list whenever a type is parameterized: valid defaults can supply omitted values. Inherited parameters are not erased merely because an extension has no new names in its own header.

requirements.definition: No parameter of the type may receive more than one type-param-spec. Every parameter without a default must have a corresponding specification. requirements.title: Positional type-parameter values precede all keyworded values
requirements.source: 7.5.9, C798, C798.omitted-keyword-condition, C798.every-preceding-omitted, C798.no-positional-after-keyword; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF106, printed92.
requirements.definition: A type-param-spec can omit keyword= only when every preceding specification also omitted it. Thus positional specifications form an initial prefix; after any keyword appears, every following specification is keyworded.

requirements.title: A parameter keyword names a formal type parameter, not a component or arbitrary object
requirements.source: 7.5.9, C799, C799.each-keyword, C799.formal-type-parameter-name; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF106, printed92.
requirements.definition: Every keyword in a type-param-spec is a parameter name of the specified type. A component name or unrelated host name does not become a type parameter keyword. Inherited formal parameters remain parameters of an extended type, subject to their actual name and ordering rules.

requirements.title: An assumed derived length parameter is confined to the three specified contexts
requirements.source: 7.5.9, C7100, C7100.asterisk-value, C7100.dummy-declaration-exception, C7100.associate-name-declaration-exception, C7100.dummy-allocation-exception, C7100.other-context-exclusion; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF106, printed92.
requirements.definition: An asterisk used as a derived type's type-param-value is allowed only in a dummy-argument declaration, an associate-name declaration, or allocation of a dummy argument. These are necessary context permissions, not waivers of the KIND-constant, SELECT TYPE or ALLOCATE constraints. In particular ALLOCATE has the additional C939 if-and-only-if condition for assumed parameters of every allocated dummy.

pending.function-result-declaration-exclusion: PENDING - Retain a source-use plan for assumed derived LEN on a function result. C727 also constrains assumed-parameter function names, and C728 adds function characteristics; establish their exact scope for the complete explicit-RESULT/declaration context before claiming C7100-only isolation. Prefer canonical ownership/reuse when coupled, rather than label a multi-constraint function negative isolated.
pending.derived-named-constant-exclusion: PENDING - Retain a conditional complete PARAMETER context with only ordinary constant-initializable components and a valid scalar constructor; the special intrinsic CHARACTER named-constant permission in7.2p7 does not extend to a derived LEN parameter. Verify all constant/constructor premises before authoring the pair.
pending.allocation-context-canonical-link: PENDING - An asterisk on a non-dummy ALLOCATE object also violates C939. Preserve canonical C939 ownership and a future source connection rather than advertise a second isolated C7100 negative. Replacing * by an expression is not a valid repair when the dummy's parameter is assumed, because C939 requires * in that case.

requirements.oracle:
Separate declaration and allocation permissions. For the positive dummy allocation, the assumed LEN comes from a compatible actual, not an inquiry of an unallocated deferred parameter. The allocation asterisk denotes its current assumed value under9.7.1.1p6.

requirements.title: Positional and keyworded parameter values correspond to the specified formal parameters
requirements.source: 7.5.9, p2.positional-no-keyword, p2.type-parameter-order, p2.keyword-present, p2.named-parameter-correspondence; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF106, printed92.
requirements.definition: Without a type-parameter keyword, a value corresponds according to type parameter order. With a keyword, it corresponds to the formal parameter named by that keyword. Conforming lists preserve C797-C799, and inherited parameters follow the parent-prefix/local-header order from7.5.3.2.

pending.nonextended-positional-order: PENDING - Assess existing S7_5_3_2_001_valid__header/reversed_statements/reversed_list witnesses and their actual independent parameter/member observations. Preserve the source primary and avoid copying a header-order program.
pending.keyword-reordering: PENDING - Plan a complete three-parameter type with distinct representable values, all keyworded in a different order, and independent observations by parameter/member name. The expected mapping is not another equally reordered constructor.
pending.mixed-prefix-and-keywords: PENDING - Plan one positional prefix followed by keywords for still-unassigned parameters in reversed order. All values and defaults remain unique; independently check the resulting parameter values.
pending.inherited-positional-prefix: PENDING - Assess existing S7_5_3_2_002_valid__parent_prefix/local_suffix/ancestor_chain witnesses at their actual scope and phase. Source-use for a whole family is not automatically a singleton link or an extra execution.
pending.keyword-name-correspondence: PENDING - Retain keyword identifier correspondence, including case-equivalent spelling, as a bounded source-use connection to lexical name rules and the actual formal set. Do not manufacture a renamed duplicate just to clear this facet.

requirements.oracle: Explicitly named parameter inquiries and defined component observations use distinct literal expectations, never equality between two potentially mis-associated constructors. Existing order witnesses require separate semantic link review for this consumer.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The paragraph specifies parameter correspondence, not component order or procedure-argument matching. A failing feature implementation does not justify replacing a planned runtime effect by compilation alone.

requirements.title: An explicit parameter value is converted to the parameter's integer kind when needed
requirements.source: 7.5.9, p2.conversion-if-necessary, p2.intrinsic-assignment-conversion, p2.parameter-integer-kind; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF106, printed92.
requirements.definition: If necessary, an explicitly supplied parameter value is converted using intrinsic-assignment rules to the integer kind declared for that parameter. For expression-valued specifications, R701 still requires scalar INTEGER, with the additional constant-expression requirement for KIND and specification-expression requirements in declarations. The * and : forms retain their separate assumed/deferred semantics, not numeric-expression admission. This is distinct from conversion of a default expression in the parameter definition.

pending.default-to-selected-integer-carrier: PENDING - Plan explicit values for KIND and LEN parameters declared with a supported SELECTED_INT_KIND carrier. Use small representable values, not the carrier's numeric code as an intrinsic kind parameter. Establish whether source/target carriers are actually distinct before claiming a conversion-path observation.
pending.selected-to-default-integer-carrier: PENDING - Plan an explicitly supplied selected-kind INTEGER constant or eligible LEN specification expression for a default-INTEGER parameter. Check the parameter's declared integer kind and independent representable value, preserving C701/C704.
pending.keyword-supplied-conversion: PENDING - Exercise an explicit valid keyword route under the same independently qualified carrier conditions; do not silently rely on a default expression that would test7.5.3.1p4 instead.
pending.distinct-kind-profile-and-canonical-use: PENDING - Review existing S7.5.3.1-001/-002 and intrinsic INTEGER conversion/profile facilities. A selector returning the default kind is not evidence of cross-kind conversion; add a separately justified profile or retain the facet pending if the necessary distinction is unavailable. No arbitrary fixed kind number or unsupported-selector compilation-as-skip.

requirements.oracle: Integer range and kind inquiries can qualify representable small values and actual carrier distinctions independently of the parameter conversion being tested. Existing default-expression conversions are not automatically explicit-use conversion witnesses.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No REAL-to-INTEGER admission, overflow-dependent result, bit-pattern assumption or circular profile using the tested parameter conversion is authorized. Failure to distinguish carriers remains visible.

requirements.title: An omitted parameter value uses that parameter's default
requirements.source: 7.5.9, p3, p3.no-explicit-value, p3.parameter-default-value; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF106, printed92.
requirements.definition: If a type parameter has no explicit type-param-value in the specifier, its value is its default. C797 requires an explicit value where no default exists. Omission does not replace explicitly supplied values, and a default expression must already be valid under R733 and7.5.3.1.

pending.omitted-kind-default: PENDING - Assess S7_5_3_1_002_valid__kind_default_positive/zero/negative as existing finite abstract-KIND omission witnesses. No duplicate cases or intrinsic representation meaning for those discriminator values.
pending.omitted-length-default: PENDING - Assess S7_5_3_1_002_valid__length_default with its actual defined parameter/member observations and source qualifications.
pending.explicit-value-overrides-default: PENDING - Assess S7_5_3_1_002_valid__expression_and_override; verify the explicit use actually bypasses the default rather than relabel a definition-only conversion test.
pending.partial-keyword-omission: PENDING - Assess S7_5_3_1_004_valid__dependent_default: its TYPE(packet(tag=5)) declaration supplies tag by keyword and omits extent, independently checking extent=6. The separate S7_5_3_1_002_valid__per_declarator case omits its entire list and is not itself a partial-keyword witness. Preserve both actual contexts instead of inventing duplicate coverage.
pending.prior-kind-dependent-default: PENDING - Assess S7_5_3_1_004_valid__dependent_default, preserving the previously declared KIND-primary condition. A prior LEN with a default is not thereby a constant-expression primary.
pending.inherited-default-source-use: PENDING - Retain the inherited-default connection to7.5.7.2 and the parent's valid parameter defaults. The earlier S7.5.3.1-002 inherited-default facet is also pending; do not cite an unwritten inherited-default program as existing evidence.

requirements.oracle: Reuse observed omission/default/override cases only after checking their actual specifier and parameter declaration contexts. All linked witnesses retain their canonical IDs, phase, profiles and independent adjudications.
requirements.oracle_limitation: R733 requires a scalar INTEGER constant default expression. A prior KIND parameter can be a constant primary in the definition; a prior LEN parameter does not become constant just because it has a default. No invented zero default for an unspecified nondefaulted parameter is permitted.
